content.text: The verifier's substantive findings all affirm the current classification: no audit right exists against Client, absence puts us above the preferred position, "missing" would be inappropriate, and the failed check is a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause. There is no defect left to repair — inventing audit machinery to satisfy the frequency check would create a TrueLink right that does not exist today, which is the opposite of the rule's purpose. I am therefore resubmitting the same compliant finding unchanged rather than manufacturing an edit.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: Confirmed compliant on re-review; no repair was required and none is made. The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Client and no access to Client systems for usage verification. This was established by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" - all nil or irrelevant) and by reading every section where such a right would conventionally sit: Compensation (§ 5-6), Client covenants and warranties (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information flows run in our favour: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. With no audit obligation binding us, our position exceeds the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: inserting audit machinery would create a vendor right that does not exist today. "Missing" is inapposite because this rule constrains a vendor-favourable right rather than requiring a protective clause. The failed "audit frequency limited" deterministic check is an artefact of the total absence of an audit clause, not evidence of a permissive one. Awareness only, not a deviation under this rule: § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, which operates on TrueLink's own Interface as an acceptable-use enforcement measure and is not an audit of our records or systems.
